evidence: no deterministic engine for strategy_id 'maxpain_brokenwing_condor_v1' (engine-registered: current_control_v1, directional_spread_v1, range_hv_iron_condor_v1)
expected_failure_modes: Trend continuation in TREND_HV drives spot through the short strikes at expiry; the wide insurance wing is breached for near its full width and such losses cluster on the highest-credit entries.
The entry gate is too restrictive (TREND_HV + VIX >= 16 + PCR <= 0.95), yielding fewer than 20 trades in the window and classifying the result NOT_RELIABLE.
Execution cost drag (40 per order across 8 legs round trip + 1.5% slippage per fill) exceeds the collected credit in normal-rich zones, leaving no net edge even when pinning behaves as hypothesized.
EOD single-timestamp OI walls diverge from settlement-week wall evolution, so the max-pain anchor drifts and the pinning advantage disappears.
hypothesis: NIFTY weekly settlement gravitates toward max pain and heavy OI walls (documented pinning: spot closes within a few points of max pain and OI walls cap the move). A defined-risk broken-wing condor whose short legs are anchored to the max-pain strike and the nearest OI walls, instead of a symmetric spot-based grid, sits on the settlement magnet rather than the mid. Entering only when the regime gate reports TREND_HV with India VIX >= 16 (rich-to-high premium zone) pays the seller for high-volatility premium while OI gravity pulls spot back toward the anchor over the weekly horizon. The asymmetric wing design caps tail risk on the trend-away side at a declared width while the premium-collecting side hugs the dense wall. It may fail because TREND_HV is a trending regime: the same flow that builds the walls can blow through them at expiry, and EOD single-timestamp walls may not represent settlement-week dynamics. No profitability claim is made here; the frozen engine, the canonical expiry calendar and the canonical cost model decide.
research_question: On the frozen window, for NIFTY weeklies, does a broken-wing condor with short legs anchored to max pain and OI walls, entered only when REGIME == TREND_HV, VIX >= 16 and PCR <= 0.95, deliver positive mean net P&L per trade after the canonical 40 per order and 1.5% per-fill slippage cost model over at least 20 trades, and is its worst-trade loss bounded by the declared wide-wing maximum loss on every entry?
title: Max-pain and OI-wall anchored broken-wing condor, gated on TREND_HV with VIX >= 16 and call-heavy PCR
